column3: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
For by it the people of old received testimony.
By faith we understand that the ages were formed by the word of God, so that what is seen did not come from things that are visible.
By faith Abel offered to God a better sacrifice than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, God testifying about his gifts; and through faith, though dead, he still speaks.
By faith Enoch was taken away so that he would not see death, and he was not found because God took him away. For before his removal he had received testimony that he was pleasing to God.
And without faith it is impossible to please him, for the one who approaches God must believe that he exists and that he becomes a rewarder of those who seek him.

By faith Noah, having been warned about things not yet seen, moved with reverent fear, prepared an ark for the salvation of his household; through this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that is according to faith.
By faith Abraham, when called, obeyed by going out to a place he was going to receive as an inheritance, and he went out not knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a foreigner in the land of promise, as in a foreign land, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, fellow heirs of the same promise.
For he was waiting for the city having foundations, whose designer and builder is God.
By faith Sarah herself also received power for the conception of offspring, even beyond the proper age, since she considered the one who promised faithful.
Therefore from one man—and him as good as dead—there were born descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven and as countless as the sand by the seashore.
According to faith all these died without receiving the promises, but having seen and welcomed them from far away, and having confessed that they were strangers and sojourners on the earth.
For those who say such things make clear that they are seeking a homeland.
And if they had been remembering that land from which they went out, they would have had opportunity to return.
But now they desire a better one, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when tested, offered Isaac; and the one who had received the promises was offering his only son,
concerning whom it had been said, “Through Isaac your offspring will be named.”
He reasoned that God was able even to raise from the dead; from there, figuratively speaking, he also received him back.
By faith Isaac also blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
By faith Jacob, when dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped while leaning on the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, when nearing his end, mentioned the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions concerning his bones.
By faith Moses, when born, was hidden for three months by his parents because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king’s decree.
By faith Moses, when grown, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh’s daughter,
choosing rather to suffer mistreatment with the people of God than to have the temporary enjoyment of sin,
considering the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking toward the reward.
By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger, for he endured as though seeing the invisible one.
By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as through dry land, which the Egyptians attempted and were swallowed up.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell after being encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who disobeyed, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
And what more shall I say? For time will fail me if I tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David and Samuel and the prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, shut lions’ mouths,
quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong from weakness, became mighty in war, and put foreign armies to flight.
Women received back their dead by resurrection. But others were tortured, not accepting release, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
Others received a trial of mockings and floggings, and even chains and imprisonment.
They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed by the sword; they went about in sheepskins and goatskins, lacking, afflicted, mistreated—
of whom the world was not worthy—wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and holes in the ground.
And all these, though having received testimony through faith, did not receive the promise,
because God had provided something better concerning us, so that apart from us they would not be made perfect.
